I have two ideas:

1) keep it simple and just do one major basic lift a time

2) borrow Weider's old 1960's mass building routine: 2 sets of 6 reps, whole body

Depends. What's the goal of your training cycle, and how many days a week?

To keep it really quick and simple, my best advice would be to get to the station for your lift and have a dumbbell or something on the side for a superset.

For instance: Bench press, rack the bar, do a set of Kroc rows, get back on the bench, repeat. Overhead press, pull ups between sets.

You can do two exercises for one muscle group if you need to focus on mass and one strength move isn't cutting it. You can do an exercise for two opposing groups (push with pull, quads with hamstrings), or you can do lower with upper.

Keep the rest times to a minimum and don't skip the two or three warm up sets. You can easily follow a canned progression system like 5/3/1 or Smolov Jr.

One way it could look: Monday: Deadlift for 5/3/1 sets. Tuesday: 5/3/1 bench superset with croc rows in the 6-20 rep range. Thursday: Squat with leg curls or KB swings. Friday: Start cycle over or go for a 20 minute jog.
